note: Built as ballot/lean/mn_endorsements.json is. Each record is one line of one party page, matched to one race and one candidate on the lists already loaded in ballot_local_2026.sqlite (office, place and name all fit, one fit only). Utah's state rows are the State Board of Education (8 contests), the Legislature (15 Senate and 75 House contests) and 62 judicial retention votes; Utah prints a party beside every State Board of Education and legislative candidate, and the retention votes carry no party. The November 3, 2026 state list carries the Republican, Democratic, Forward and Constitution parties, unaffiliated candidates and declared write-ins. Utah's county, city and school district contests are not loaded (the state publishes no list of them; each county clerk certifies its own), so a party line about one of them is unmatched with that reason. No Utah party page read for this file calls anything an endorsement for a 2026 state or local race, so 'endorsements' is empty. Under 'other_support', with the page's own wording in 'kind' and never to be shown as an endorsement: the Utah Republican Party's '2026 Republican Candidates'; the Utah Democratic Party's 'Common Sense Candidates' (organizeutah.org, which the 'Our Candidates' link on the party's own site opens and which says it is paid for by the Utah Democratic Party; the page also asks for a no vote on Amendment B, a ballot question, not recorded); the Forward Party of Utah's '2026 Candidates' and the national Forward Party's release of September 1, 2026 naming the same 21 Utah candidates; the Constitution Party National Committee's 'Meet the Candidates', whose Utah section lists the Constitution Party of Utah's candidates; and the candidate pages of county parties: the Salt Lake, Davis, Summit, Washington, Weber, Wasatch, San Juan, Iron, Tooele and Cache County Democratic parties, and the Washington, Davis, Cache and Wasatch County Republican parties. Only office and name were taken from each page; the biographies, priorities, quotations and links on these pages were not recorded. Every one of these candidates is on the ballot under that party's own label, so a line adds nothing to the party printed on the ballot, with two exceptions: the Forward Party of Utah's page lists, marked 'Independent', Alan Wessman (SH64) and Patrick Belmont (SH3), who are on the November list as unaffiliated; the national Forward Party's release lists them too. No party page read names a judge on a retention vote. The same candidate often stands on several lists (the state party's and a county party's): count a candidate once per party. Lines matched although the page spells the name differently keep the page's spelling in 'as_listed' (Lilian Bowles for Lillian Bowles; Nastassja Grossman for Natassja Grossman; Rebecca Windsor for Rebecca Winsor; and names given without a middle initial, or with a shorter given name, such as Ron for Ronald M Winterton). Read on 2026-10-03 with the kit's honest User-Agent, each site's robots.txt checked first (none forbids these pages); every page in 'lists' was opened a second time and a record kept only if the page still showed the name (none was lost). Social media pages were not read. Things for a person to decide: nothing needs deciding for the page. For John's information: news reports (search results, not opened) say the Utah Republican Party's chair urged delegates at the April state convention to vote against retaining Justices Diana Hagen and Jill Pohlman (Justice Hagen has since resigned; Justice Pohlman's retention is on the November list); no party page read publishes that position, so nothing is recorded for it.
